items.title: Mayoral candidates to debate issues impacting businesses in Mississauga
items.summary: Mississauga’s four main mayoral candidates will meet on the debate stage in two weeks in the downtown core to present their plans for addressing key issues impacting the city’s business community. The top four polling candidates — incumbent Carolyn Parrish, former mayor Bonnie Crombie and city councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla — will square off as the Mississauga Board of Trade hosts its 2026 Mississauga Mayoral Debate on Sept. 25 at the Sheridan College Hazel McCallion Campus. m. Theme of the event is “business and leadership,” according to the board of trade, which represents some 1,000 larger businesses in addition to numerous smaller operations across Mississauga. Mayor Carolyn Parrish, at right, and former mayor Bonnie Crombie will debate key Mississauga business issues on Sept. 25. The Mississauga Board of Trade describes the upcoming debate as “an important conversation about Mississauga’s future” and adds it will provide an opportunity “to hear directly from mayoral candidates” as they discuss issues of most importance to city businesses of all sizes. “Whether you’re a business leader, entrepreneur, professional or engaged member of the Mississauga community, this is an opportunity to hear the candidates’ perspectives and learn more about their vision for the city,” MBOT said in an online notice of the debate. In-person attendance is exclusively available to MBOT members, “offering members a unique opportunity to experience the debate live and engage with the discussion in person,” organizers said.

items.title: Controversial condo project deferred in Mississauga
items.summary: A controversial Mississauga condo project has been deferred. Residents came out to oppose the project at 900 Lakeshore Rd. W. in Lorne Park this week. The property is next to Richard’s Memorial Park, currently home to a single-detached house with a pool. The revised plans to build a nine-storey condominium apartment building with 161 units came to the City of Mississauga’s Planning and Development Committee on Sept. 8. After community members made delegations opposing the current plan, the committee voted in favour of deferring the project. The development plans have long been the subject of opposition, with residents holding a rally against the so-called “cruise ship” condo in 2025. While there have been several changes to the plans, including reducing the height and size of the building, there are still many concerns, particularly because the development is next to beloved natural areas. The wetland and natural heritage features will be protected, and water and sewer infrastructure can be made available, Mississauga City Planner Paul Stewart said at the Sept. 8 meeting. The building lot is on a slope, but it will remain stable, Stewart said. However, councillors and residents wanted more details on how the new building would mitigate environmental concerns.

items.title: Fireworks complaints kept to a minimum over long weekend in Mississauga
items.summary: Long weekends during the summer typically keep Mississauga bylaw enforcement officers busy responding to incidents where fireworks are either used or sold illegally. And the City of Mississauga complaints line normally fields dozens of calls from residents drawing attention to the same issues. Not this past weekend, though, as city officials say only six fireworks-related complaints were received from the public over the Labour Day weekend. In addition, no fines were issued for improper use of fireworks or illegal sale of the devices. com. Prior to the final long weekend of the summer, city officials reminded residents last week that backyard fireworks displays were not permitted in Mississauga on Labour Day weekend unless residents first got the go-ahead from the city. Celebrating with fireworks anywhere in the city on any day throughout the weekend, including the holiday Monday, required a permit. As usual on holiday weekends, Mississauga bylaw enforcement officers were out in full force to ensure fireworks weren’t being sold or used illegally. In Mississauga, fireworks displays are only allowed at home without a permit on Victoria Day, Canada Day, Diwali, Lunar New Year and New Year’s Eve.

items.title: Ontario, Canada announce up to $401 million for Mississauga housing infrastructure
items.summary: 4 million in funding to help Mississauga build infrastructure needed to support new housing, including major transit projects. The funding is being provided through the Development Charges Reduction Program, which helps municipalities that have reduced development charges invest in infrastructure required to accommodate growth. Mississauga was among the first Ontario municipalities to substantially reduce development charges, with reductions of up to 100 per cent aimed at encouraging housing construction and improving affordability. The city has committed to maintaining those reductions until March 31, 2029. The funding will support housing-enabling infrastructure, including a new zero-emission transit maintenance and storage facility and a downtown transit mobility hub. As Canada’s seventh-largest city, Mississauga plans significant investment in transit infrastructure is needed to support its growing population and new housing development, including a new zero-emission transit maintenance and storage facility on city-owned land at 7300 West Credit Ave. The city projects transit ridership will rise by 50 per cent by 2035, requiring an additional 250 buses. MiWay currently operates from the Edward J. Dowling Transit Facility and the Malton Satellite Facility. Both are at full capacity, limiting the system’s ability to expand its fleet and improve service. The city is also planning a new Downtown Transit Mobility Hub as Mississauga’s downtown continues to grow.

items.title: Home at last! Dozens of shelter pets find their fur-ever homes
items.summary: Strong community support helped dozens of cats and dogs find loving homes, including long-term shelter residents waiting since 2023. When the Mississauga Animal Services shelter reached capacity for dogs in August 2026, a call for community support led to 53 animals finding positive outcomes. During the shelter’s Homeward Bound adoption event, 18 dogs, 22 cats, seven rabbits, five birds and one mischievous python were adopted, placed in foster homes or transferred to nearby rescues. Between August 8 to 22, adoption fees were reduced to $25 plus HST for all dogs and cats. This limited-time promotion offered significant savings compared to regular adoption fees, which are typically $280 plus HST for dogs and puppies and up to $190 plus HST for cats and kittens. Community response was immediate. The shelter received over a hundred calls a day and dozens of visitors. Seven dogs were adopted on the first day of the event, while cats were adopted so quickly that many found homes the same day they became available. The success of the Homeward Bound event has helped ease capacity at the shelter and freed up space for other animals in need of care. Some of the most heartwarming stories came from long-term shelter residents who finally found their forever homes after months, and in some cases years, of waiting. For shelter staff and volunteers who cared for these animals, watching them leave with their new families was one of the most rewarding moments of the event.

items.title: Ward 5 Councillor Says Year-Old Goreway Bridge Has Ended Decades of Rail-Crossing Gridlock
items.summary: According to INsauga, Mississauga's Ward 5 Councillor Natalie Hart says the $40-million Goreway Drive Overpass has delivered real benefits to residents, businesses and drivers in the year since it opened. The outlet reports the four-lane structure, built above CN's rail line in Malton near Toronto Pearson Airport, took its first vehicles on October 15 of last year after decades of gridlock along the corridor connecting Mississauga and Brampton. INsauga reports Hart called the overpass incredibly important to her community in several ways, not just for daily commuters. According to the outlet, she said the bridge has improved traffic flow along Goreway Drive as well as other north-south arterial roads in the area. INsauga reports Hart said drivers no longer get stuck waiting at the tracks while trains move goods through the community. According to the outlet, she added that the change has been good for both local businesses and residents.
